segments.text: The page lists text files through a file parameter, and the View sourcecode link is disabled. So the source has to be recovered through the bug itself.
I fetch the page and grep for links. Only the three stylesheet links come back — no source link, no file list.
I use the bug to read the source itself. I pipe cat of the index.pl file through the file parameter, dodging the filter with a glob, and grep for the interesting lines.
The program takes the file parameter, and if it contains the word natas it prints a mocking message. Otherwise it opens the input with dot txt appended, using the two-argument form of Perl's open.
In the two-argument form, if the string begins with a pipe, Perl does not open a file. It opens a pipe to a shell command, and the command's output goes into the response.

And the filter is just a pattern match on the word natas, while the shell expands wildcards. N question mark tas matches natas after glob expansion but does not contain the word itself, so the check passes.
I prove execution with id. The command runs as natas29.
Then I list the webroot. It holds the index.pl and the perl underground text files.
Finally I cat the password file directly, again with the glob: slash etc slash n question mark tas underscore webpass slash n question mark tas thirty. It prints the password for natas30.
